reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight of adjusted plus-minus lies in decomposing observed goal differentials into individual player contributions while controlling for confounding factors such as line-mate quality and opposition strength. This requires addressing two major statistical challenges: multicollinearity from frequent pairing of players and low event frequency in hockey. Ridge regression addresses multicollinearity by introducing L2 penalty on coefficients, shrinking them towards zero without eliminating any variable. By incorporating shot-based metrics like Fenwick and Corsi, which are more abundant than goals, the model gains statistical power and reduces estimation error. These enhancements allow for precise quantification of player impact across various game states—especially even strength, power play, and shorthanded situations. The resulting estimates are expressed in goals per 60 minutes, providing a standardized measure of offensive and defensive value. The derived operators form a coherent mathematical framework for GSI’s Bayesian inference pipelines and GSE’s tactical simulations.
